collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 40 or older)

collection.description: A villager lies awake wondering if they would make their biggest choice again: decide yes, probably, or decide they do not know.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (name1) is lying awake, asking (him/her)self a question (he/she) has never quite asked before: if (he/she) could go back to the biggest choice of (his/her) life, would (he/she) make the same one? (He/she) knows which choice it was. (He/she) thinks about it until the frogs stop singing.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: Yes, probably. Not because it all went well; it didn't. Some of it was very hard. But the hard parts came with the good parts, tangled up together, and (he/she) can't pull them apart. "Yes," (he/she) whispers to the dark, "but I'd do some of it differently." That seems like an honest answer. (He/she) falls asleep at last.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (He/she) can't decide. Some nights the answer is yes. Some nights it's no. Some nights it's "the other way would have been just as good, and just as hard." (name1) realizes (he/she) might never know, and that it doesn't change anything either way. (He/she) made the choice. (He/she) lived it. (He/she) turns over and goes to sleep.
